issue: The statement says every corrected-grid certificate of accuracy eps, including its filtering history, has a last-stage grid with at least 1+1/(2 sqrt eps) nodes per coordinate. The proof uses only the filtering rule with threshold U >= OPT = 0, which never removes an interval. A valid path certificate (Def def:cert) may remove any interval whose endpoint min-marginals are >= beta, and here beta < 0. Exact counterexample: n=2, F=(x1-x2)^2, eps=1/50. Stage 0 is the uniform grid of step 1/5 on [0,1]^2, where all min-marginals are -1/50. Stage 1 is the box [0,1/5]^2 with grid {0,1/5}^2, where min Q = -1/50. With beta=-1/50 and xhat=0, (C1) and (C2) hold and the gap is eps, yet the last grid has 2 nodes instead of the claimed >= 4.54.
